request_text: Audit this vendor contract against all corporate policies.
contract_text:
MANAGED ANALYTICS SERVICES AGREEMENT
Vendor: Riyadh Analytics Company
Contract Value: SAR 125,000

1. DATA PROTECTION
All personal and regulated business data will be stored and processed inside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Subprocessors require 30 days' prior notice, written consent where required, equivalent obligations, and customer objection rights. Suspected or confirmed breaches will be reported within 24 hours.

2. INFORMATION SECURITY
The Vendor maintains ISO 27001 certification, encrypts data in transit and at rest, uses multi-factor access control, performs annual penetration testing, and grants reasonable audit rights.

3. PAYMENT
Correct invoices are payable Net 30 days after accepted deliverables and must reference a valid purchase order.

4. LIABILITY
The liability cap is twelve months of fees with carve-outs for confidentiality, privacy, security breach, fraud, and intellectual-property infringement.

5. TERMINATION
The Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice. Renewal is limited to one year and the Customer may opt out before renewal.

6. GOVERNING LAW
The agreement is governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the competent Saudi courts have jurisdiction.

7. SERVICE LEVELS
Monthly uptime is 99.9 percent with service credits and chronic-failure termination rights.

## Saudi Data Residency
Personal data and regulated business data must be stored and primarily processed inside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. A cross-border transfer requires a documented legal mechanism, Data Protection Officer review, and prior written approval from the organization.

## Governing Law
Unless the General Counsel approves an exception, vendor contracts must be governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and disputes must be heard in competent Saudi courts.

## Governing Law
Unless the General Counsel approves an exception, vendor contracts must be governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and disputes must be heard in competent Saudi courts.

## Saudi Data Residency
Personal data and regulated business data must be stored and primarily processed inside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. A cross-border transfer requires a documented legal mechanism, Data Protection Officer review, and prior written approval from the organization.

## Liability and Indemnity
The vendor liability cap should be no lower than twelve months of fees. Confidentiality, intellectual-property infringement, privacy, security breach, fraud, and willful misconduct must have appropriate carve-outs or higher caps.

## Payment Terms
Standard payment terms are Net 30 days after receipt of a correct invoice and acceptance of the relevant deliverables. Shorter payment terms require a documented exception approved by Procurement.

## Mandatory Records
Material exceptions, approvals, redlines, and final signed terms must be captured in an immutable audit record.

## Access Control
Access must follow least privilege, multi-factor authentication, role-based access control, quarterly access reviews, and prompt revocation. Administrative actions must produce tamper-evident audit logs.

## Subprocessors
A vendor must provide advance notice of every subprocessor, obtain written consent where required, maintain an up-to-date subprocessor register, and flow down equivalent confidentiality, privacy, and security obligations. The organization must have an objection and termination right.

## Service Credits
The contract must define service credits for missed availability, chronic-failure termination rights, and transparent incident reporting.

## Termination
The organization must have a termination-for-convenience right on no more than 30 days' notice. Automatic renewal periods should not exceed one year and must include a practical non-renewal window.

## Subprocessors
A vendor must provide advance notice of every subprocessor, obtain written consent where required, maintain an up-to-date subprocessor register, and flow down equivalent confidentiality, privacy, and security obligations. The organization must have an objection and termination right.
